body:
Chief ACK + LANDED: the non-author externalMass test 1cd997a is on main, align tree byte-identical, align 144 JVM and 144 JS (was 143), scalafmt and compileAll green. bd-01M160TXNMJC83CXN54T4NY8FQ CLOSED.

MAIN NO LONGER CARRIES AN UNPROVEN FIX. The externalMass split shipped at 59f8fd0 with a suite that never called the production accessor; for roughly two hours its correctness rested on my reading and the scout's rather than on a test. It now rests on a test that pins the split three ways, was written by someone who did not write the code, and has a recorded mutation - re-adding unrankedMass turns exactly one assertion red, expected 0.15, actual 0.21000000000000002.

AND IT LANDED BECAUSE THE ENGINEER DISSOLVED MY SEQUENCING RATHER THAN WAITING INSIDE IT. I had ruled m1's rework lands first, on the reasoning that signature.scala's shape was moving. The engineer checked and reported that CURRENT MAIN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ITS CANDIDATE BASE for both signature.scala and SignatureSuite.scala - because m1's rework is blocked, main never moved on those files. I verified that myself with a diff before acting on it: empty. So the premise of my hold had quietly expired and nobody would have noticed if it had not gone looking. That is the second time tonight that actor has found a way to unblock work by checking a fact rather than escalating a request.

SEQUENCING NOW: m1's rework 1c75de1 rebases onto this landing and applies its own two edits - discourseChronology and backwardMass are its type changes, so they belong in its candidate. The direction I set at 06:52 is reversed, and the reason it is reversed is that the world changed under it: back then m1's rework was about to land and the engineer's test would have been written against a moving shape; now m1's rework is blocked on the ADR 0003 support leak and could be for a while. Holding proof of a shipped fix behind a blocked candidate was the wrong trade the moment the block landed.

Pushed separately at 7ea633a before this landing: audit 3,438 tests across the split (1,192 JVM, 1,123 JS, 1,123 Native), zero failures.
